meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. People draft in other programs and paste it in. And you still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. Is that the only thing you have?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misremember lines all the time. "That line isn't in the play" is a misquote, not a finding. Is there anything else on paper?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Arguments change between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. I'll read both documents myself, side by side.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you spoke to him the day before the zero. A seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher can freeze on a question. Put that note in writing, with the date on it.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A timed forty minutes against a weekend at a desk is not the same task. Every student writes better with time. What are you actually proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good. Procedure 4.3 says software alone establishes nothing, and I'd have said so. I asked what you are proposing.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Fine. A rewrite, to put this behind him, private and not in front of his class. I want 4.4 in writing tonight, with nothing on his record, and the rest goes in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. When is the rewrite? It has to be done before December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
I'll check with Owen and put the day in my email. Send me your options in writing tonight, with 4.4 and the promise about his record.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. That's what I'm holding you to, tonight, in writing.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
No. The rest goes in my email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: the principal

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero, nothing on Owen's record, and confirmation of that in writing from you tonight. I still expect your scheduling options in writing so the rewrite happens this week and the new mark is in well before December 1, and I will confirm Owen's day once I have them. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite that replaces the zero, with nothing on Owen's record and your confirmation in writing tonight, and she still wants your scheduling options in writing and the rest of her points in her email; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You offered to let her check the version history on your screen and said you were describing what it showed, not why, which gave her something she could verify herself.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero up front, and when you mentioned the checker score you said you were not leaning on it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence of the text arriving close to midnight the night before the due date came near that night, which is why her answers got shorter there, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided on the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen, answer both directly in your next breath, since your conversation with him the day before was your strongest reply to her procedure complaint and she had to wait for it.
